original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact paid-call minimum for diag([xyx],[xyx],[e],[e]) in M4(F2[S3]) with two restored dirty scalar roles, paid labels {x,y} and all 120 rank-one idempotents of M4(F2). Answers open question 1 of research/s3-three-role-xyx (PR #4084): a fourth role does not lower the six-call minimum.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the three-register obstruction. This package fixes the nonabelian S3 alphabet of PR #4084 and increases the dirty role count from three to four for its one target; it is a finite exact minimum, not a new operation alphabet or a supplier.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the bit register model: tests whether more restored dirty workspace compresses one nonabelian S3 target. A shorter word would still need a native supplier map before any kappa consequence; none is claimed.
stop_rule: Exclude every word of length 0..5 over the 240 paid factors by exact involution meet-in-the-middle, verify the direct six-call word, calibrate the engine on the three-role layer sizes and stop. Do not extend to five roles or other targets.
evidence: verify.py: Phi = (rho, sign) is checked to be an algebra isomorphism F2[S3] -> M2(F2) x F2[C2]; three-role ball layers [1,56,1750,45396] match the pinned PR #4084 certificate; four-role ball(I,2) layers [1,240,32650] agree with an independent M4(F2[S3]) engine under Phi; zero hits for ball(I,3) cap T*ball(I,2); length-4 and length-5 positive controls hit; direct six-call word exact, each one-call omission misses.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a fifth or any larger number of restored dirty roles lower the six-call minimum for diag([xyx],[xyx],[e],...)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three and four roles give six; a uniform statement for every role count would close the workspace question for this target.
open_questions.first_step: Try a uniform argument in the M_{2m}(F2) rho block, where the search shows four roles already need six calls; the transvections there have the restricted shapes (u(x)p)(v(x)q)^T.
open_questions.blocked_by: Five roles give 992 factors and a ball(I,2) of up to about 5 x 10^5 states (estimate, not computed), which is slow for this pure-Python meet-in-the-middle; no uniform proof is known.

open_questions.question: Is the rho quotient alone enough for every role count?
open_questions.why_it_matters: At four roles the M8(F2) image already has no length-5 hit, so the C2 block is not needed; a proof in GL_{2m}(F2) would be a cleaner certificate.
open_questions.first_step: Characterize products of at most five restricted transvections that act as the partial swap on two coordinate planes.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only a finite four-role observation is available.
